editorial:
If you miss the days when spy movies were gritty, fast, and full of double-crosses, this one will feel like a welcome throwback. Pierce Brosnan plays Peter Devereaux, a retired CIA agent pulled back in for a mission that turns deeply personal. Before long, he is hunting and being hunted by his own former student, which gives the whole story a tense mentor-versus-protege edge. The plot moves through Europe, mixing political conspiracy, Russian power plays, and shadowy agency secrets, so there is always another layer to uncover. It is not reinventing the genre, but it keeps you guessing and delivers plenty of shootouts and chases along the way.

Brosnan is the main reason to watch, bringing a cool, dangerous charm that makes every scene feel sharper. The action is solid and the pacing rarely slows down, though the story can get a little tangled with all its twists and side characters. If you enjoy old-school spy thrillers with a darker tone, this is an easy recommendation. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final act, Devereaux discovers that the Russian president-elect is hiding a dark secret involving a war crime, and that CIA officials are covering it up to protect their own interests. His former student, Mason, is ordered to kill him, but Devereaux turns the tables and exposes the truth. Mason ultimately chooses to walk away rather than finish the job, letting Devereaux go. The movie ends with Devereaux reuniting with the woman he was trying to protect, having cleared his name and brought the conspiracy into the light, though the cost of the mission leaves him more isolated than ever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school spy thrillers and Pierce Brosnan.
